the_stale_work_on_disk: Ten chapter files for 745 to 754 were already on disk when this block was begun. They were a form, not ten scenes: every one of them opened with the same two sentences, put the whole chapter on one visitor standing at one edge, ran a dialogue in which the person inside the house recites an inventory of what is shut, folded, leaning or leaning still, refused a refusal, and closed on the same hand lifted in a farewell. Two chapters of them share eight lines of dialogue word for word, including the pair of exchanges You are short today / I am short, and the two both close on the man or woman staying at a door until the sound goes from the lane. Their own band file declared the family as somebody coming as far as the edge of somebody else's place and no further, and admitted in the same file that this was close enough to 665 to 674 to need testing. That is the position of the block that was meant to be third, and it is 665 to 674 again. All ten files were replaced. Nothing of the plot, no date, no band and no standing object was taken from them, and the two things downstream that needed them are given back in 0749 and 0750. The old files are recoverable from git and were not read for anything but their own defects.
question_put_to_a_human: What are chapters 745 through 754 about, in one sentence? Put to a human before this file was written, as it has been put before every writer since 595. No human has answered it for any block from 595 onward. No writer answers it for them. It is recorded here unanswered and it stays open until somebody answers it.
family: DECLARED BEFORE ANY CHAPTER OF THIS BLOCK EXISTS, AND IT IS A WRITER'S POSITION AND NOT A HUMAN'S ANSWER. In these ten days, in five houses, work that belongs to one person gets done by somebody else. Not offered and not asked for. Done properly, done in front of the person whose work it is, and neither of them ever puts a word to it, so that by the end of the block each of these five people is doing less than they were doing in July and none of them can say when that started. Nobody is kept at a door. Nobody is put to work. Nobody is measured, priced, added up, told, carried, written down, waited for or refused. A job simply crosses from one pair of hands to another in the middle of an ordinary day and nobody in the room remarks on it.
family_why_this_and_not_the_last_three: 0054 took none, ten scenes each standing alone, and gave its reason. 0055 took one built on a figure that does not agree with the thing it measures. The stale work on disk for this block took a third thing, which was where a person is permitted to stand, and that third thing was 665 to 674 with the furniture changed, and the review of 0057 has already ruled against it in the handoff for 0058, which says in so many words that a writer may not argue a new family position off a claim about edges. So there are three positions in a row and this is not any of them. This one is not about where anybody stands and not about a number. It is about whose work it is. The test of a position is not whether it is defensible. It is whether it is the same one taken last time, and this one has been taken never.

cards.0745: A woman of seventy-eight finds that her sister has been putting the bin out at the kerb and bringing it back for a fortnight, lets her do it again that day without one of them mentioning that she knew, settles a washday for the Wednesday after, and goes on at a kitchen table with nothing on it.
cards.0746: A man in his early forties finds the loose post at his own yard gate packed with wire driven down the split from the top down, works out that he cannot undo it without taking the post out, tells a woman from two doors down that her mother can have the key out of his own drawer and put it in her own porch himself, hooks the latch back over the gate and does not touch the post.
cards.0747: A woman in her late forties opens the back of her own van for the first time since the spring for a woman who books work, finds a strap has come off its ring on the board rack, binds it with fencing wire she has carried in her apron since April before anybody can offer, refuses the woman an afternoon twice, gives her the invoice pad, and lets the hall line go back empty.
cards.0748: A woman in her late fifties finds there is no broom in that house, turns the front step over on a Sunday morning after being told twice it cannot be done on a Sunday, finds forty years of paint on the underside and an old empty nest in the low corner, puts the nest back in the corner when the step is back down, and carries the shopping bin up her own front path and down it again rather than let it be carried for her.
cards.0749: A woman in her early thirties finds the dustpan at the foot of her own wall emptied and stood out by somebody, tells a boy over the fence to stop doing her yard without telling her, empties the trough by hand with six buckets in the middle of the day for the first time since May, says out loud that the ninety yards are not a distance she is refusing on principle, and hooks the latch back over her own gate.
cards.0750: A woman of seventy-eight's yard path has not been swept in ten years and there is no broom in that house. A woman calls at the back door to say in person what she has been refusing by letter, sees the path, sweeps it, and is neither stopped nor thanked for it; the woman puts her own bin out at the kerb by hand for the first time since the middle of July and goes on inside.
cards.0751: A man in his early forties sweeps his own bench first thing and finds it swept again in the middle of the day with his own shavings lying on the clean part, answers a woman from two doors down who is sweeping her own path across the lane, tells her he is not taking the wire out of his own gate post, leaves the shoulder on a length of oak scribed and not cut, carries his own bin out to the kerb for the first time since the spring, and sweeps the bench again over the top of what somebody else had done.
cards.0752: A woman in her late forties refuses a woman who books work an afternoon twice and refuses her a sash window off a job she did in June twice, tells her why once each time and will not say either again, puts the window into the roof of her own greenhouse on her own, writes the address of that bungalow on the underside of it in pencil, and says nothing to anybody about any part of it.
cards.0753: A woman in her late fifties finds a key to her own front door on a split ring in the bottom of the shopping bag, gives the woman who put it there two reasons for not having it and uses the word preference when she is told a preference is not a reason, puts the ring into an envelope and the envelope into a drawer while the woman is still on her step, and watches her carry the bin up the path and back down it again without having asked her to.
cards.0754: A woman in her early thirties tells a boy over the fence that she is not going to be asking him for anything ever again and he says she can, finds the dustpan full and empties it herself, puts his ball back over the fence at him instead of down the garden, hears a strip of ply come off her own shed in the first wind, carries it back up the yard and stands it again at the same angle against the same loose felt, and does not go out to it.

movement: Nothing is rescued. The freeholder does not arrive. No plate is unscrewed and no wire is spliced and nobody rings through to anyone who can act. The ladder is not opened and no room is painted. The box behind the bench is not opened. The drawer with leads and screws is not opened. The front room at twelve is not entered. The report is not chased. The envelope is not turned. The drawer at ten is not opened. The ninety yards are not walked. The hall line stays empty. The brush on the runner at twelve is not lifted. What moves in the ten is other people's work, and it moves quietly, and it does not move back.
two_person_meetings: Eight of the ten have two people in a room or at a door. 0746 and 0751 put the two people apart, one at a roller door and one at a gate and one across a lane, and in 0746 nobody is let past the door track. The pair at number nine in 0748 and 0753 is the same pair twice and the two are deliberately not a pair of visits in the same manner: in 0748 the woman is let in and the whole business happens indoors and out to the far side of the house, and in 0753 she will not come inside and the whole business is through the open door and once in the back yard, and she ends by using the bin without knocking. The woman at twelve in 0745 and the woman who sweeps the path in 0750 are not the same figure and the two are not compared anywhere in either chapter.
closing_images: Ten different ones, corrected to the prose. 0745 a bin turned back the right way up against a wall and the kettle on the ring again. 0746 a bolt dropped into its keeper, the latch hooked over it, the post untouched, the pencil back behind the ear. 0747 a rack shaken as hard as it will shake and not moving, and then out to the tip with a barrow. 0748 a nest pressed back into the low corner of a turned step with the ball of a hand. 0749 the flags swept at the back step, the brush put away, the shed door shut, the gate left as she left it. 0750 a woman standing in a kitchen with a bare table who does not go out and look at the path. 0751 a roller door pulled down to belt height and a man standing in the half-dark with a clean bench behind him. 0752 a whole greenhouse thrown up on a yard wall by the light under a roller door, with one bright square in it, and a woman standing in the middle of her own yard looking at that. 0753 a woman on a step that does not rock, looking down a front path at the front of her own house where the bin is not. 0754 a woman in a doorway watching a strip of ply come down and settle and stand there, and not going out to it. One chapter ends on a thing put away, 0745, and one on a thing left where it is, 0753, and no chapter repeats either.

FACT, thirty-one findings, all fixed: the sister no longer goes out through a gate she does not go out through; the sister leaves once and comes back once; the gate at twelve is propped back since September and the latch exchange is gone; the lamp is over the gate; 0745's caps now says Wednesday; 0746 no longer knows what hour the wire went in and carries both a latch and a bolt; 0746's bench sweep lost its hour so that 0751's morning sweep is the fixed one; 0747's strap was never snapped and is not now; 0750 leaves the trough until the boy has gone; 0751's shoulder is scribed and not cut and the word collar is gone, and 0761 uses the same word; 0752 was rebuilt from the middle down and the sash is now on the boards outside, then in the roof, then locked; the woman in the home is no longer in the house being cleared; the hole in the roof is the protagonist's to point at; 0752's caps now say she tells her why once and will not say it again; 0753's key is in the envelope on screen and the envelope in the drawer on screen and never on the table after; the cardigan is one business and the closing cardigan is gone; 0749's dustpan and 0754's are consistent because she stands it back her own way; three caps blocks corrected to their own bodies on 0752, 0753 and 0754; 0754 now returns the ball over the fence, which both its caps line and its card had promised and the body had not staged. review_of_0056_and_what_this_repair_corr.nothing_restarted: No chapter was rewritten. No date was moved, no family was changed, no band was changed, no standing object was changed, no planned turn was changed, and seven of the ten chapters were not touched at all. Two chapters were touched in one exchange each and in one clause.
in_the_prose: 0745 ran two speeches together in one paragraph, a complaint from the sister and the protagonist's question, and they are now two paragraphs. It was the only such join in the twenty chapters of the two newest blocks.

0745 gave number twelve a washing line, and canon puts the line and the too-tight shed-end peg at number ten, where 0729 pegs it straight and where the line is bare. The sentence that did it was also garbled, two subjects and since before Christmas twice. The protagonist's own line is gone. She now has nothing to hang washing on and cannot get to the far end of her own yard with her hands full, which is the same obstacle the sentence was reaching for, and the sister brings her own line over from her own house and puts it up across the back of the yard on the Wednesday. The washday, the four sheets, the forty minutes, the four sentences, the near end and the far end, and the line I am not doing your washing all stand. **Number twelve has no washing line and never had one. The line at number ten is untouched and is a different line at a different house with the shed-end peg still too tight, and a later writer must not move either.**

0759 dated the undoing of the latch at number ten to a time before the summer, and 0749 says in terms that nobody has ever been on the other side of that latch in the time she has had the yard. An absolute and a since cannot both stand. 0749's absolute is the load-bearing image and is quoted in the continuity file and in this band file, and 0759's clause was the weaker of the two, so 0759 now says the latch has not had anybody on the other side of it in this yard in the time she has had it, which is the same fact in the chapter where she breaks it. The unlocking in 0759 is now the first time, which is what 0759 was written to be, and the scene is otherwise untouched.
